title: Concurrent API key creates with one name answered 500: the insert's unique violation was not mapped to the 409
summary: On dev at 01:02:04Z two `POST .../organizations/<org>/api-keys` requests with the same name, sent in the same millisecond by a flow-suite run, both answered 500 `Unexpected error`. The service checks the name before the insert, so both requests passed the check and the second insert hit `organization_api_keys_organization_id_name_key` (23505), which the service mapped to `fault.ErrUnexpected`. A new concurrency test found the same 500 on 13 of 14 public create or rename routes. anchor#237 maps each unique violation to the 409 the pre-check already returns; it is live on dev. Prod carries the same latent race until the next anchor prod deploy.

impact.text: Dev only: two API key creates from the CI flow suite answered 500 instead of 201 and 409. The same race existed on 13 of 14 create or rename routes in prod; no prod occurrence was logged.

numbers.label: routes failing the new race test

trigger: Two same-name API key creates for one organization reached anchor dev in the same millisecond.
detection: The 500s and the 23505 error rows were in PostHog logs at once. A parallel session opened the fix (anchor#237) 40 minutes later; the daily `posthog-error-watch` routine triaged the rows at about 11:15Z. No alert fired for two isolated dev 500s, which is fine at this volume.
resolution: anchor#237 maps the unique violation on every create or rename with a name pre-check to the existing 409, with a concurrency test per route; merged 11:21Z and live on dev.

events.label: Check-then-insert name rule in the initial anchor snapshot
events.detail: `organization_api_key_service.go` `Create`: `nameUniqueValidation`, then the insert inside a transaction; any insert error becomes `fault.ErrUnexpected`.

events.label: Two same-name creates answer 500 on dev
events.detail: `jet: pq: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "organization_api_keys_organization_id_name_key" (23505)` logged by the repository and the service, then `Internal server error: Unexpected error`.

events.label: No further 500s: the suite run moved on
anchor#237 opened with the fix and the race test

whys.problem: Two concurrent creates of an API key with the same name answered 500 instead of one 201 and one 409

because.text: The second insert hit the unique constraint, and the service turned every insert error into `fault.ErrUnexpected`
because.evidence: Log rows at 01:02:04Z (23505 on `organization_api_keys_organization_id_name_key`); `organization_api_key_service.go` `Create` returns `fault.ErrUnexpected` on any transaction error.

because.text: The 409 came only from a name check run before the insert, so two requests could both pass it
because.evidence: `nameUniqueValidation` runs outside the insert transaction; a concurrent writer's row is invisible until it commits.

because.text: The service treated the database constraint as unreachable once the pre-check passed
because.evidence: Only the license services matched 23505 (`pgerr.IsUniqueViolation`), added after their own incidents.

because.text: No rule or shared helper required a pre-check's insert to map its unique violation to the same 409
The same 500 waited on 13 of 14 public create or rename routes, in prod as well as dev
because.evidence: `TestConcurrentSameNameWritesReturnConflict` failed 13 of 14 cases on the old code (anchor#237).

because.text: No test ever sent concurrent writes of one name; every test created names one at a time
because.evidence: The race tests in anchor#237 are the first concurrent-write tests for named resources.

because.text: The test suite had no concurrency case for unique names, so the class stayed hidden until a flow suite raced it

contributing: The same class caused the 2026-10-07 duplicate Clerk reconcile incident (anchor#211); that fix stayed local to the reconcile path.

Two leftovers need a different fix than a 409: concurrent inbound webhook deliveries on `integration_events_..._external_event_id_key` and concurrent email template draft/publish version numbers (listed in anchor#237).

well: Both the repository and the service logged the constraint name, so the cause read from one row.
The fix swept the class with a concurrency test per route instead of patching one endpoint.
wrong: A check-then-act pattern sat in the codebase since the first snapshot, and the earlier 23505 incident did not trigger a class-wide look.
lucky: A CI flow suite raced the route on dev before any customer did on prod.
The endpoints already declared 409, so the fix needed no contract change.

actions.what: Map every pre-checked unique violation to the existing 409 with `OnUnique`, 12 resources (create and rename)
Rule in `docs/development/agent-rules.md`: a pre-check's write maps the unique violation and adds a race-test case
Fix the two leftovers: idempotent inbound webhook event insert, email template version race
Deploy anchor#237 to prod (prod still on 48bdb77)

messaging.internal: Two same-millisecond API key creates on anchor dev answered 500 (unique violation after the name pre-check). anchor#237 maps it to 409 on 12 resources with race tests; live on dev, prod pending deploy.
